texts.preamble: Smt. Jyoti vs Sh. Sandeep @ Monu (Husband) on 14 October, 2022 In The Court Of Sh. Yashwant Kumar Principal District & Sessions Judge, North West District, Rohini Courts, Delhi Crl. Appeal No. 116/2022 Cnr No.DLNW010081962022 Smt. Jyoti W/o Sh. Sandeep D/o Sh. Ramphall R/o H. No. Wp122, Ashok Vihar Wazirpur Village Delhi110086 ....Appellant Versus 1. Sh. Sandeep @ Monu (Husband) S/o Late Sh. Vishnu Bhagwan 2. Smt. Shakuntala (Motherinlaw) W/o Late Sh. Vishnu Bhagwan Both R/o H. No. 30, Gali No. 2 Harijan Colony, Bhalaswa Village Delhi ....Respondents Date of filing : 17.08.2022 Date of arguments : 07.10.2022 Date of Judgment : 14.10.2022 Judgment
texts.facts: 1. The appellant has filed this criminal appeal under Section 29 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (hereinafter referred to the "said Act") against the ex parte judgment dated 23.05.2022 (hereinafter referred to the impugned judgment) passed by Ld. MM-01 (Mahila Court), North-West, Rohini Courts, Delhi in a complaint case bearing Ct. Case No. 19004/2016, whereby the Ld. Trial court vide the said CA No. 116/2022 Jyoti V. Sandeep @ Monu & Anr. Page No. 1 of 13 impugned judgment, directed the respondent No.1- herein/husband to pay a sum of Rs.3,000/- pm towards the maintenance of the petitioner-therein/appellant-herein till the time she is legally entitled to be maintained by him as per law. The respondent No.1/husband was also directed to provide an alternate accommodation to the petitioner/appellant according to the standard of living maintained by her in the matrimonial home or to pay rent in lieu of alternate accommodation to the petitioner/appellant, subject to placing on record rent agreement and rent receipts. Vide the impugned judgment, the Ld. MM declined the prayers of the petitioner /appellant for protection order and custody of the minor children. The respondent No.1/husband was also directed to pay Rs.5,000/- in total to the appellant/wife as compensation for the harassment Smt. Jyoti vs Sh. Sandeep @ Monu (Husband) on 14 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147201041/ 1 suffered by her due to domestic violence as well as for loss of time and money spent in prosecuting the said application. 2. The brief facts, as set out in the present appeal, are that marriage between appellant and respondent No.1 was solemnized on 07.12.2007 as per Hindu rites and ceremonies and from the said wedlock, two children namely Himanshu and Kartik were born. The appellant-wife filed a complaint u/s 12 of DV Act against the respondent No.1-herein and his family members. In the said complaint case, the appellant-herein alleged that she was physically assaulted, tortured and beaten up by the respondents-therein for not fulfilling their illegal demand of dowry. The appellant-herein/wife has also alleged that respondent-herein failed to make any provision for maintenance to her despite the fact that he has sufficient source of income of Rs.2,50,000/- pm from his businesses including illegal works CA No. 116/2022 Jyoti V. Sandeep @ Monu & Anr. Page No. 2 of 13 and rental income of Rs.20,000/- pm. The appellant-herein sought various reliefs in her application/petition u/s 12 of the said Act. In the said complaint case, summoning qua respondent Nos. 4 and 5 were declined vide order dt. 02.12.2016 and respondent Nos. 1 to 3 were proceeded ex parte vide order dt.12.12.2018. After the ex parte evidence of the appellant-wife, the final arguments on behalf of the appellant- herein/complainant-therein were heard and Ld. Trial Court passed the impugned judgment dt. 23.05.2022. 3. Aggrieved by the said impugned judgment, the appellant has preferred the present appeal on the grounds among others that the impugned judgment was passed in mechanical manner and without going into the merits of the case. The respondent No.1 is a man of means as he owns a meat shop at Jahangir Puri, Delhi from which he is earning around Rs.1,50,000/- pm apart from rental income and income through other illegal means and in order to mislead the Ld. MM, the respondent No.1 took the defence that the said meat shop does not belong to him and same is being run by some other person. Ld. MM has not taken into consideration the material placed i.e. photographs etc. and passed the impugned judgment. As per the circular of State Government in the year 2022 regarding minimum wages, the minimum wages of semi-skilled labours have been increased from Rs.17,693/- to Rs.18,187/- pm and for skilled workers, the wages has been increased from Rs.17,743/- to Rs.20,019/- pm. The maintenance of Rs.3000/- pm is very meager amount considering the status and income of the respondent No.1. The respondent No.1 deliberately and intentionally with sole intention to harass and humiliate the CA No. 116/2022 Jyoti V. Sandeep @ Monu & Anr. Page No. 3 of 13 appellant, wants the appellant to live in a Jhuggi in a slum area as he has refused to arrange a suitable rented accommodation for the appellant. The respondent-herein is not allowing the appellant to enter into her matrimonial home and the appellant is being forced to live at a rental accommodation which is not habitable in any manner and moreover such place is not right for the safety and security of the appellant. The respondent may be directed to permit the appellant to enter into the matrimonial home. The real and actual income of the respondent No.1 is more than Rs.2,50,000/- pm. The appellant has prayed to [LEAKAGE_MASK] the impugned judgment dt. 23.05.2022. 4. The respondents-herein have filed reply to the appeal and raised the preliminary objections that the Ld. MM has rightly passed the impugned judgment dt. 23.05.2022 after hearing the parties. The Smt. Jyoti vs Sh. Sandeep @ Monu (Husband) on 14 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147201041/ 2 present appeal has been filed by the appellant in order to harass the respondents. In reply to brief facts and grounds, the respondents also stated that the appellant made a false story in order to implicate the respondent No.1 in frivolous cases and to create false and frivolous evidence against the respondent No.1-herein. It was the appellant who time and again used to leave the matrimonial home and that too without informing the respondent No.1 and other family members. Not only this she never cared about the children. The appellant has taken false and frivolous pleas in order to take advantages of her own wrongs. The other averments made in the present appeal against the respondents have been denied by the respondents in their joint reply to the appeal. The respondent No.1 runs a meat shop. The respondent No.1 is earning Rs.1,50,000/- pm apart from rental income. His total monthly income is Rs.2,50,000/- and he is living luxurious life. The photographs of the meat shop placed on record were not considered by the Ld. MM. Even the minimum wages for semi-skilled labours in Delhi has been increased from Rs.17,693/- to Rs.18,187/- pm but a meager amount of Rs.3,000/- pm was awarded as maintenance. The respondent No.1 is involved in several criminal activities. The respondent No.1 has not arranged a rented accommodation for the appellant in compliance of the judgment dt. 23.05.2022 and threatened her that she will be forced to live in a Jhuggi. As per the judgment in the case of Satish Chandra Ahuja Vs. Sneha Ahuja in Civil Appeal No. 2483/2020 (arising out of SLP No. 1048 of 2020), an aggrieved person must be given rental accommodation at her matrimonial home by the husband when the rental accommodation for the appellant is not safe for her life and safety. The appellant/wife is a house-wife and has no source of income. 7. The appellant has not filed any case for custody right of the children. The appellant-herein/wife has made allegations of domestic violence against the respondents-herein and his family members in her complaint/petition filed before the Ld. Trial Court. Summoning qua respondent Nos. 4 & 5- therein were declined vide order dt. 02.12.2016.
texts.arguments: 6. Ld. Counsel for the appellant argued that the marriage of the appellant was solemnized on false pretext by saying that the respondent No.1 is a government servant but he is involved in illegal activities. She was subjected to cruelties and beatings. Ld. Counsel for the respondents argued that the appellant never performed her part of obligations towards the CA No. 116/2022 Jyoti V. Sandeep @ Monu & Anr. Page No. 5 of 13 respondent No.1 as well as her children. It is the appellant who on her own left the matrimonial home without informing the respondents on 24.12.2015. The children were aged about 3 and 7 years respectively when the appellant/wife left her matrimonial home. The children are studying in 7 th and 4th standard. 10. I would place a reliance upon the judgment reported in the case of Bhuwan Mohan Singh Vs. Meena & Ors. 2014AIR (SC) 2875, wherein it was held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court on the concept of sustenance and obligation of husband that the concept of sustenance does not necessarily mean to lead the life of an animal, feel like an unperson to be thrown away from grace and roam for her basic maintenance somewhere else. T h e petitioner-therein/appellant-herein alleged that the respondent No.1-herein/husband is earning a total income of Rs.2,50,000/- pm from his business of meat shop, rental income and other illegal business. 12. In the case of Sh. Bharat Hegde V. Smt. Saroj Hegde, 140 (2007) DLT 161, the Hon'ble Delhi High Court in para No. 6 held that " While considering a claim for interim maintenance, the court has to keep in mind the status of the parties, reasonable wants of the applicant, the income and property of the applicant. Conversely, requirements of the non applicant, the income and property of the non applicant and additionally the other family members to be maintained by the non applicant have to be taken into all. Whilst it is important to insure that the maintenance awarded to the applicant is sufficient to enable the applicant to live in somewhat the same degree of comfort as in the matrimonial home, but it should not be so exorbitant that the non applicant is unable to pay. The Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in para No. 19 of the judgment in the case of Bharat Hegde (supra) further held that "As noted herein above, unfortunately, nobody pays proper taxes to the Government. Self employed persons seldom disclose their true income. Prudence and worldly wisdom gained by a judge before whom citizens of all stratas of society litigate it can always be used Smt. Jyoti vs Sh. Sandeep @ Monu (Husband) on 14 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147201041/ 5 by a Judge to broadly ascertain as to what is going on in the society. By no means, said knowledge can be used where law requires a fact to be conclusively proved. But where the law requires a Judge to form an opinion based on a host of primary data, a Judge can formulate an opinion pertaining to the likely income from the capital assets of the husband". 13. In the case of Sujit Kumar V. Vandana in MAT. APP. (F.C.) 35/2015, the Hon'ble Delhi High Court held that "Where the parties do not come forward with exact income they have, the Court would have no alternative but to apply its guess work. In the decision CA No. 116/2022 Jyoti V. Sandeep @ Monu & Anr. Page No. 10 of 13 reported as 140 (2007) DLT 161 Sh. Bharat Hegde Vs. Smt. Saroj Hegde, it was held that under noted eleven factors have to be taken into account:- 1. Status of the parties. 2. Reasonable wants of the claimant. 3. The independent income and property of the claimant. 4. The number of persons, the non applicant has to maintain. 5. The amount should aid the applicant to live in a similar life style as he/she enjoyed in the matrimonial home. 6. Non-applicant's liabilities, if any. 7. Provisions for food, clothing, shelter, education, medical attendance and treatment etc. of the applicant. 8. Payment capacity of the non applicant. 9. Some guess work is not ruled out while estimating the income of the non applicant when all the sources or correct sources are not disclosed. 10. The non applicant to defray the cost of litigation. 11. The amount awarded Under Section 125 Cr.PC is adjustable against the amount awarded Under Section 24 of the Act". 14.
